agent_notes: מָלָךְ is a perfect verb. I render it 'reigns' in the dramatic layer and 'has reigned / is king' in the literal layer; the enthronement-shout reading ('YHWH has become king!') is a scholarly choice, not stated in the packet's commentaries. Meiri reads the perfect as prophetic ('past for future'); the plain sense here follows the surrounding present-tense hymn.

agent_notes: זָרֻעַ 'is sown' is the reading of the Masoretic text. Meiri notes it may be a variant of זָרַח 'dawns' (his letters ח/ע exchange); I do not rely on this and keep 'sown', which Rashi and Ibn Ezra support in the packet. I did not cite the ancient versions, which are not in the packet.
Radak glosses זֵכֶר קָדְשׁוֹ simply as 'his name'. ASV 'holy memorial name' follows that line; I keep 'remembrance of his holiness' literally and flag the name reading in the commentary.
Revised per the reviewer: the commentary now says the KJV pluralizes עָנָן only, and that its plain 'darkness' loses the specific sense of עֲרָפֶל; the claim that both nouns are pluralized is gone.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses רָאֲתָה as 'it sees' and וַתָּחֵל as 'it trembled'. I kept 'saw' and 'writhed' for the pair, because the sequence (perfect, then wayyiqtol) is narrative-past. חוּל is the verb of labour pains and of whirling; Rashi cites the birth sense (Ps 48:7; Mic 4:9).

agent_notes: Tense: הִגִּידוּ is a perfect and וְרָאוּ a waw + perfect, so past ('declared ... saw': YLT, ASV 'have seen') and present (KJV) are both possible. I kept the literal past and the dramatic present; the commentary no longer says the KJV flattens the tenses.

agent_notes: אֱלֹהִים in 'all gods' is disputed: the packet's Radak, Metzudat David and Meiri read it as the host of heaven; Ibn Ezra records some who take it as angels; the Targum reads 'all peoples who serve idols'. I translate 'gods' and discuss the options in the commentary. The perfect/imperative form הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ is formally imperative (STEPBible morph), though Radak and Meiri take it as past-for-future.
